name: Cueing effect
fact: Adding visual cues that relate elements of a picture to the text raised retention scores in a learner-paced classroom study, but the same study reports only a weak cueing effect that does not easily generalise to non-laboratory settings.
grade_basis: Corpus evidence = one primary study (Tabbers, Martens & van Merrienboer 2004; 111 participants; one classroom experiment). The model asserted B+ from a BACKGROUND span restating cognitive load theory's prediction; that span was discarded and the record re-anchored to the paper's own RESULTS and CONCLUSIONS. C rather than C+ because the single source calls its own cueing effect weak and reports the companion modality effect REVERSING in the same experiment, so the direction survives contact with the data but the magnitude and the generality do not. Grade reflects OUR corpus provenance, not the literature at large; to be re-graded when the computed rubric (D-114) lands.
